slides.title: Scramble it
slides.text: Encryption scrambles a message so only someone with the key can read it. Decrypting turns it back.
slides.alt: Secret Messages in Pro: the cipher wheel waits with a scrambled message only the key can open.

slides.title: A shift of 3
slides.text: A shift cipher moves every letter along the alphabet. The key is how far to shift.
slides.alt: The wheel at work: letters are shifting along the alphabet by the key, turning plain words into code.

slides.title: Brute force
slides.text: A shift has only 25 keys, so you can try them all. That is brute force. A keyed substitution has so many keys that trying them all takes far too long.
slides.alt: A later cipher level: with so few keys, trying every one is a real way in — for a shift cipher.

slides.title: Hiding is not scrambling
slides.text: Steganography hides a message, for example in a picture's pixels. Anyone who finds it can read it. Encryption makes it unreadable without the key.
slides.alt: Steganography: a heart hidden in a picture. Each pixel is a number, and its last bit says dot or blank, so the picture looks the same.

slides.title: Faked senders
slides.text: A trick message can fake its sender name. That is spoofing. It may also use facts from a public profile to seem friendly.
slides.alt: A Pro trick card: the sender name looks friendly, but a faked name is exactly what spoofing means.

words.means: scrambling a message so only the key opens it
the secret that scrambles and unscrambles

slides.title: Pim's piece lights up
slides.text: Three pieces lit. Pim bows, and the Spark glows brighter still. One world is left: Gizmo the mouse is waiting inside the machine, where everything is very, very small.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Packet Post at Secret Messages and finish all 7 levels with the key wheel. Then the game sends you to Spot the Trick: check the 4 trick cards there for faked senders.
slides.alt: Secret Messages in Pro: the cipher wheel waits with a scrambled message only the key can open.
